newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITV calls for cut in licence fee payments.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITV calls for cut in licence fee payments.

text.p: A leading ITV executive urged the UK government on Tuesday to cut the 400 million stg annual bill which ITV's 15 members pay the treasury.

"Four hundred million pounds is not sustainable. ITV will not be able to deliver quality public service TV as required (unless there is a reduction)," ITV Association director Barry Cox told a conference organised by the left-leaning Institute for Public Policy Research.
"If we maintain that level of taxation through the next 10 years (ITV) companies will become unprofitable," Cox added.
The ITV companies pay for their broadcast licences with a fixed annual cash sum plus a percentage of advertising and sponsorship revenue.
The treasury receives around 400 million stg from the payments but there are huge differences between what is paid by each licensee.
Carlton Communications Plc, for example, pays a cash element of around 45 million stg for its London licence but only 2,000 stg for its Central TV operation in the English Midlands.
The cash bid was part of the original licence application in 1991. Companies who faced no opposition for their licenses were able to table nominal bids.
ITV companies can apply to have their 10-year licences renewed from 1999 and a number of them are lobbying the Independent Television Commission (ITC) watchdog for a reduction in licence payments.
They note that cable and satellite companies such as BSkyB Plc are not included in the system.

ITV company Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television has urged the government to introduce a standard duty payable by all commercial TV operators. They say this would not result in any loss of revenue to the treasury.
